evidence: Abstract: 17 versions of Azure networking APIs, 14 regressions, 5 in specs, 9 in services. Sec 4.3: service regressions show the service update 'since the latter [spec] remains constant'. Sec 4.4: 'Regressions #6 to #14: Unspecified Properties in Responses.'
correction: Godefroid, Lehmann, Polishchuk, ISSTA 2020 (DOI 10.1145/3395363.3397374). Precise: 17 versions of Azure DNS/Network APIs (2016-2019). The 9 service regressions are #6-#14 in Table 2 and Sec 4.4, all unspecified response properties.

evidence: Sec 4/RQ1: 'identified 251 versions that have introduced breaking changes ... remaining 219 (87.3%) ... did not specify any information related to deprecation'. Abstract: 'only 3 out of 219 studied deprecation-related RESTful APIs adopt a proactive method' (HTTP headers/error code).
correction: Yasmin, Tian, Yang, arXiv:2008.12808 (2020). The 3/219 figure is in the Abstract and RQ4-Findings, not RQ1. The 219 are deprecation-related APIs, so do not call them simply '219 APIs'. Note the coincidence that 219 is also the 87.3% numerator.

evidence: Additive list includes 'Adding a response field' and 'Adding enum values'; 'Any additive (non-breaking) changes will be available in all supported API versions.' 'Removing enum values' is listed as breaking.

Additional updates table: 'Removes the `charges` attribute from the `PaymentIntent` object | Payments | Breaking'; 'Adds new decline codes to the PaymentIntent and PaymentMethod APIs | Payments | Breaking'.

Special cases table, ISK: 'ISK transitioned to a zero-decimal currency, but backward compatibility requires you to represent it as a two-decimal value ... to charge 5 ISK, provide an amount value of 500.' UGX row has the same text.
correction: Say 'documented only in human-readable docs (a Special cases table), not machine-readable' rather than 'only in prose'. Calling it a '100x unit trap' is our own interpretation, not Stripe's wording.

evidence: Limitations > Data freshness: 'Don't use search for read-after-write flows ... because the data won't be immediately available to search. Under normal operating conditions, data is searchable in under 1 minute.'
correction: Stripe does not use the term 'eventually consistent'. Paraphrase as 'search results lag writes (normally under 1 minute)'.

evidence: 'Specify the API version in your SDK': 'Versions of stripe-python before v6 use your account's default API version.' Account default version 'defines ... the structure of API responses' and is set in the Dashboard.
correction: The same applies to stripe-ruby before v9, stripe-php before v11 and stripe-node before v12. The Dashboard-upgrade consequence is an inference from the default-version definition, not a quoted sentence.

evidence: Under 'Release schedule': 'If your app targets an inaccessible version, Shopify falls forward and responds using the oldest accessible stable version.' But responses include an X-Shopify-API-Version header 'reflecting the version used to fulfill the request.'
correction: Drop 'silently'. Requests to retired Shopify versions fall forward to the oldest accessible stable version. The only signal is the X-Shopify-API-Version response header, and the response body does not flag it. Location is the 'Release schedule' section, not a 'Fall forward section'.
